correctness.rationale: Expanding the exact published penalty with \(\varepsilon=e^{-\lambda d}\) gives \(g(\bar n/\varepsilon)=[\ln(\bar n/\varepsilon)+1+O(\varepsilon)]/\ln2\) and \(h_2(\varepsilon)=[\varepsilon\ln(1/\varepsilon)+\varepsilon+O(\varepsilon^2)]/\ln2\). Substitution yields the stated coefficient. Logarithmic inversion gives the continuous cutoff law; integer rounding contributes only \(O(1)\), and the prime number theorem preserves the leading prime-cutoff scale. The complexity corollary is direct substitution into the source's \(O(d^2m\log m)\) bound. The claim explicitly limits itself to the published certificate.

value.rationale: The new pure-loss construction is capacity-achieving only after sending its finite-dimensional cutoff to infinity. Quantifying that limit turns a qualitative 'exponential' statement into an explicit rate-versus-dimension and rate-versus-decoder-cost law. The \(\ln\ln(1/\delta)\) correction identifies the polynomial entropy-continuity prefactor, while the leading prime-cutoff and \(\log^2(1/\delta)\) decoder factor give a usable accuracy budget. This is a natural resource question tied directly to the new coding construction, not an arbitrary reparameterization.
